issues.description: The problem statement and some task descriptions refer to a method named getFeedingSound(), while the UML and the intended design use an abstract method named messageOnFeed() on Animal. The solution implementation also defines and uses messageOnFeed(). This name mismatch between getFeedingSound and messageOnFeed is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which method to declare/implement and which method Farm should call when feeding animals or singing the song.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the method name across all artifacts. Either (A) change all references to getFeedingSound() in the problem text and template to messageOnFeed(), or (B) rename the abstract method in the UML/solution to getFeedingSound() and update Farm and animal classes accordingly. Ensure the template Farm and the song/spec call the same method name so students know which method to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the feeding-sound method as getFeedingSound() in several places, while the UML, the task that defines the abstract method, the template expectations, and the solution implementation use the name messageOnFeed(). This mismatch (getFeedingSound vs. messageOnFeed) can confuse students about which method they must implement and call (e.g., in feedAllAnimals()), causing unnecessary cognitive load and potential compilation/runtime errors if they follow the incorrect name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement to messageOnFeed(), or (B) rename the abstract method and its implementations in the code (Animal, subclasses, and Farm) from messageOnFeed() to getFeedingSound(). Prefer (A) to align with the UML and existing solution (messageOnFeed()).
